description:
Usage and approximate spend on the AMD internal LLM gateway, scraped from the reporter on amd-laptop (10.0.0.107:9876, job amd-llm-exporter).

Read every number here as a window total, not a rate. The reporter republishes the gateway's own 30-day rolling report (amd_llm_window_days), and publishes it as a gauge -- so rate() and increase() are meaningless on these series, and a value that falls has not lost data, it has aged out of the back of the window. Anything labelled "per day" on this dashboard is a same-series offset, which is net of that ageing; see the panel description.

The charge figures are the gateway's own approximation, not an invoice.

panels.description: API requests in the reporting window. Unfiltered by the Provider/Model pickers -- this is the gateway's own total, and it is the figure the per-model table should sum to.
panels.title: Requests

panels.description: Total tokens in the reporting window, across every model and provider. This counts far more than prompt + completion: see the Token Mix panel for what the difference is.
panels.title: Total Tokens

panels.description: The gateway's approximate charge for the window. Approximate is the operative word -- it is list-price arithmetic over the token counts, not a bill, and it does not know about any internal rate or credit. Treat it as a size, not an amount owed.
panels.title: Approx Charge

panels.description: Blended price per million tokens across the whole window. This is the one number that moves when the *mix* changes rather than the volume -- a week of Opus pushes it up, a week of Haiku or of heavy cache reuse pushes it down.
panels.title: Cost / 1M Tokens

panels.description: Approximate charge divided by request count. Agentic traffic makes this large and lumpy -- one Claude Code session is many requests, each carrying the whole conversation forward -- so read it alongside Cost / 1M Tokens rather than on its own.
panels.title: Cost / Request

panels.description: Length of the gateway's reporting window, straight from amd_llm_window_days. Every total on this dashboard covers exactly this much history regardless of the time range picked above -- the range only controls how much of the *reporter's* history is charted.
panels.title: Reporting Window

panels.description: Approximate charge per model and provider for the window. The same model served by two providers is two bars on purpose: the gateway routes between AzureOpenAI and VertexGenAI, and the split is the only visibility into that routing we get.
panels.title: Approx Charge by Model

panels.description: Share of window spend. Useful for the question the bar chart answers badly: whether spend is concentrated in one model or spread across the fleet of them.
panels.title: Share of Spend

panels.description:
Each model's window-total charge, charted over time. A line that climbs steadily is a model in active use; a line that flattens has stopped being called and is coasting on history still inside the window; a line that falls is that history ageing out.

A new model appears here as a line starting at zero only if it is genuinely new. A model the gateway has served all along but which the reporter has only just started breaking out will appear at full height.
panels.title: Window Charge by Model

panels.description:
Day-over-day change in the window total: value now minus value 24h ago.

This is NET, not spend. The window is rolling, so it is (what was charged in the last day) minus (what aged off the back of the window). On a steady workload it sits near zero even though real money is being spent, and it can go negative after a busy day drops out 30 days later. Read it as "am I trending up or down against a month ago", never as a daily bill.

increase() is not an option here: these are gauges, and Prometheus would treat every window-ageing decrease as a counter reset.
panels.title: Net Charge Change vs 24h Ago

panels.description:
Every (provider, model) pair the reporter breaks out, for the whole window.

"Other" is total tokens minus prompt minus completion. It is not a rounding error -- it is the overwhelming majority of the token count, and it is what the gateway's own total charges for while the prompt/completion fields describe only the uncached part of each call. Cache reads are the plausible explanation; the reporter does not label it, so neither does this column.

The queries join on a synthetic `key` label built by label_join, because seriesToColumns takes one field and this table is keyed on two.
panels.title: Per-Model Breakdown

panels.description: Request count per model and provider for the window. Compare the shape of this against Approx Charge by Model -- where they disagree is where an expensive model is being called rarely, or a cheap one constantly.
panels.title: Requests by Model

panels.description:
Where each model's tokens actually are. Prompt and completion are the fields the reporter names; Other is total minus those two, and on this gateway it dwarfs both -- typically well over 99% of the count. Almost certainly cache reads, which is what makes the blended Cost / 1M Tokens as low as it is.

The bars are stacked, so the full length is that model's Total Tokens.
panels.title: Token Mix by Model

panels.description: Each model's window-total token count over time. Same reading as Window Charge by Model: slope is activity, flat is coasting, falling is history ageing out of the window.
panels.title: Tokens in Window by Model

panels.description: Each model's window-total request count over time. The cleanest place to see a routing change: a line going flat while another starts climbing is the gateway moving traffic between providers or model versions.
panels.title: Requests in Window by Model

panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape the reporter at all. Green here says the HTTP endpoint answered -- it says nothing about whether the numbers it served are current. Last Successful Fetch is the panel that does.
panels.title: Exporter

panels.description: Age of the reporter's last successful fetch from the gateway API. This is the panel that catches the failure `up` cannot: the reporter serving a stale cached report indefinitely while answering every scrape happily. Thresholds are deliberately loose because the gateway report itself updates slowly -- yellow at 1h, red at 6h.
panels.title: Last Successful Fetch

panels.description: Fetch failures in the last 24h. Unlike everything else on this dashboard this one really is a counter, so increase() is the right operator. A non-zero value with a green Last Successful Fetch means it retried and recovered.
panels.title: Fetch Errors (24h)

panels.description: Fetch errors per hour, charted. A flat zero is the expected state; a step means the gateway API rejected or timed out, which is worth correlating against a plateau in the Spend panels above.
panels.title: Fetch Errors

title: AMD LLM Metrics
